SMTO-BOOT-0029 — The installer can't read the latest vLLM release's build details

GUID: 3d0e6432-819a-43fd-9d20-0e730fad2d7b
Slug: boot-vllm-cuda-metadata-unknown
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer reads the newest vLLM release's details online to pick the build that fits your graphics card. That release no longer lists them the way the installer expects, so it stopped before installing vLLM.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy the full terminal output, including the vLLM version number named in the message. The maintainer needs that exact version to update the installer for the new release.
  2. Send it to the person who maintains your SMTO copy and ask for an updated vLLM installer. Only an updated installer can read the new release's details; the problem is in the installer, not your computer's setup.
  3. When you have the updated installer, run conda env list. If the environment name from this attempt is listed, use a new name or remove that half-built environment, then install again. This attempt already created the environment without vLLM, and the installer won't install into an existing name.

What success looks like

  • The updated installer prints "Selected vLLM" with a version and CUDA backend, then installs it.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0029 line, to the person who maintains your SMTO copy. Don't install a vLLM version or CUDA build by hand to get around this; a mismatched build may not work with your graphics driver.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • vllm_install_support.py select_wheel found no VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION: str = "major.minor" declaration in vllm/envs.py at the release tag for the latest PyPI version, so it cannot tell which CUDA build the unsuffixed wheel targets.

What this means

  • The selector cannot extract VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION from the tagged release's source metadata. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • The selector cannot extract VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION from the tagged release's source metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact tagged source/version and parser expectation instead of guessing a toolkit.

How to fix it

  • Inspect vllm/envs.py at the tagged release on GitHub and update the VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION pattern in select_wheel (src/vllm/vllm_install_support.py) to match how that release declares its default CUDA build, verifying against the published wheels. The plan step runs after environment creation, so remove the partial environment or use a new name before reinstalling.
  • Inspect the tagged release metadata and update the selector for a verified supported build.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A maintained selector verifies the release's actual supported CUDA metadata.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
